terms.gloss: catch up with, reach in time; catch (a bus or train)
terms.grammar: with the accusative: autoraedam longam assequī
evidence: Cic. Att. 3.5: sī enim es Rōmae, jam mē adsequī nōn potes
terms.comment: Classically of overtaking someone on the road by hurrying (Lewis & Short: “with the idea of active exertion”). Said of a bus or a train it is our use. For getting on, īnscendere.

phrases.latin: Currendum est, sī autoraedam longam assequī volumus.
phrases.english: We’ll have to run if we want to catch the bus.

phrases.latin: sī enim es Rōmae, jam mē adsequī nōn potes; sīn es in viā, cum eris mē adsecūtus, cōram agēmus quae erunt agenda
phrases.english: if you are in Rome, you can no longer catch me up; but if you are on the road, when you have caught up with me we shall settle face to face what has to be settled
